content:
# Introduction to RAG

## Welcome to AI Memory

Imagine a student taking a final exam. 
The student sits in the exam hall. 
The student is not allowed to open any book. 
The student must write every answer using only memory. 
This is called a closed-book test. 
Normal AI models work in the exact same way. 
An AI model is a computer program that learns human language. 
It stores facts inside its internal connections. 
These internal connections are called neural network weights. 

## The Problem: Why AI Forgets and Hallucinates

A normal AI model reads a lot of text during training. 
It learns patterns from this training data. 
However, this training data stops at a certain date. 
The AI cannot check new facts on the internet. 
It has strict knowledge limits. 
Sometimes, the AI does not know the true answer. 
Instead of staying silent, the AI invents a false answer. 
This false answer looks very real. 
We call this bad habit a hallucination. 
A hallucination is a fake answer made up by the AI. 
We need a way to stop these hallucinations. 

## The Solution: What is RAG?

RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. 
RAG is like an open-book exam for an AI model. 
The AI is given a book or a document to read during the test. 
It looks at the document to find the correct answer. 
RAG connects the AI to an external knowledge store. 
An external knowledge store is a file or a folder outside the AI model. 
RAG does not change the internal connections of the AI. 
It leaves the neural network weights completely frozen. 
It only fetches new text from the outside world. 
This design makes RAG very cheap and fast. 

## Worked Example: College Admission Chatbot

Let us look at a simple example from India. 
You want to join a local college. 
The college releases a new admission notice PDF circular. 
The PDF contains exact dates for fee payment. 
You ask an AI chatbot a question. 
You ask, "When is the last date to pay fees?" 
A normal AI model will guess the date. 
It will likely give you the wrong date. 
A RAG system will solve this problem easily. 
The RAG system reads the PDF circular first. 
It finds the exact fee date in the PDF. 
Then, it gives you the correct date. 

## Step 1: Preparing Knowledge with Chunking

A college PDF circular is very long. 
An AI model cannot read the whole PDF all at once. 
We must cut the large document into smaller pieces. 
Chunking is the process of splitting a large text file into smaller paragraphs. 
Each small paragraph is called a chunk. 
Chunking helps the AI read text very easily. 

## Step 2: Understanding Meanings with Embeddings

Computers only understand math numbers. 
They do not understand English words directly. 
We must convert text chunks into numbers. 
Embeddings are secret number codes that capture the core meaning of sentences. 
Similar sentences get numbers that are close to each other. 
This helps the computer match questions with correct answers. 

## Step 3: Storing and Finding Data in a Vector Database

We must save all these numerical vectors in a safe place. 
A vector database is a special digital filing cabinet that stores these number codes so the computer can search through them very fast. 
It stores millions of text chunks as numbers. 
When you type a question, the database compares your question numbers with the stored numbers. 
It finds the most matching text chunk very quickly. 

## Step 4: The Search Process (Retrieval)

Retrieval is the exact step of searching the database to find relevant text chunks. 
The system takes your question. 
It searches the vector database. 
It pulls out the best matching paragraph from the college PDF. 
It ignores all other unrelated paragraphs. 

## Step 5: Combining Question and Context (Augmenting the Prompt)

Now the system has your question and the retrieved paragraph. 
Augmenting the prompt is the process of appending the retrieved passages directly into the prompt along with the user's question. 
The prompt is the instruction text given to the AI. 
The system gives the AI a new instruction. 
It says, "Read this paragraph and answer the user question." 

## Step 6: Delivering the Answer (Generation)

Generation is the final step where the AI writes a clear response for the user. 
The AI reads the retrieved paragraph. 
It writes a simple and polite sentence. 
It tells you the exact last date to pay your college fees. 
This answer is safe and true. 
It also shows the source document name. 
This is called provenance. 
Provenance means showing the exact origin of the information. 

## Why RAG Reduces Hallucinates

RAG stops the AI from guessing. 
The AI relies on the retrieved source text. 
If the text says the date is Monday, the AI says Monday. 
This grounds the answer in real facts. 
Factual errors drop down to a very low level. 

## Limitations and When RAG Fails

RAG is very powerful, but it has flaws. 
RAG has a retrieval bottleneck. 
This means if the retrieval step fails to find the correct chunk, the AI cannot answer. 
The AI will still fail if the external document is missing the facts. 
Also, searching databases takes a small amount of extra time. 
This extra time is called latency. 

## Summary

- RAG is an open-book method for AI models.
- It fixes knowledge limits and stops false answers.
- It uses chunking to cut long files into small parts.
- It uses embeddings to turn words into math numbers.
- It stores numbers in a vector database for quick search.
- Retrieval finds the best matching text.
- Prompt augmentation combines the question and the retrieved text.
- Generation writes the final correct answer.
- RAG does not change the core AI model weights.

## Self-Check Questions

1. What is the main difference between a normal AI model and a RAG model during an exam analogy?
2. Why do we need chunking before putting text into a vector database?
3. Does RAG retrain or change the internal neural network weights of the base AI model?
